items.title: Live: James in halfpipe medal hunt as Japanese rider stuns with big score
items.description: Scotty James and Valentino Guseli are striving to add to Australia's medal tally in the men's halfpipe final, after Josie Baff stormed to a famous gold medal. Follow live.

items.title: Baff's self-belief a blessing with a gold medal payoff
items.description: Self-belief is the most powerful tool at an athlete's disposal, and Josie Baff utilised it to its fullest extent with a magical run to gold in the 2026 Winter Olympics snowboard cross.

items.title: After just nine months Sussan Ley was sent on eternity leave
items.description: The issue for the Liberal Party is not simply the toppling of a female leader. It's also about what happened to that leader while she was in the job.

items.title: Tony Abbott issues Taylor a warning on what not to become
items.description: As Angus Taylor takes the Liberal leadership via a spill motion, a former leader with plenty of experience offers up some advice on dealing with One Nation and immigration.

items.title: What we know about Angus Taylor's policies
items.description: The new Liberal leader has signalled he will pursue a stricter immigration policy and a return to "Australian values" in his first pitch to win back voters.

items.title: Fancy parties and crude emails reveal the entertainment world's ties to Epstein
items.description: Some of the celebrities mentioned maintained friendships with Epstein even after his 2008 conviction for soliciting underage sex.

items.title: 'Sickening': Courtney's doctor did seven surgeries that experts say she never needed
items.description: Pathology from Courtney's seven surgeries with Dr Simon Gordon repeatedly showed no signs of endometriosis. The surgeries left her medically infertile.

items.title: Elections are reshaping global politics
items.description: At a time when so much of the global conversation is about the rapid decline of democracy, it is striking what a huge impact elections are having on world events just now.

items.title: The very unusual factor in the Nancy Guthrie missing person case
items.description: What initially seemed like a high-profile kidnapping that might be resolved with a multi-million-dollar bank transfer has now morphed into something else.

items.title: Torvill and Dean's Bolero produces ice dance perfection at Winter Olympics
items.description: Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean were already hot favourites for a gold medal. But on the ice in Sarajevo, the British ice dancers provided a performance of perfect artistry that made Olympic history.

items.title: Nine people killed in Canada mass shooting identified
items.description: Six children and two adults were killed in the shooting in the remote Canadian town of Tumbler Ridge on Tuesday.

items.title: US aircraft carrier redeployed from Caribbean as Iran tensions rise
items.description: The United States will send the USS Gerald R. Ford aircraft carrier to the Middle East amid escalating tensions with Iran, according to US media outlets.

items.title: 'Holiday in a can': Why Japanese beer is suddenly everywhere
items.description: As record numbers of Australians continue to visit Japan, Japanese brewers have come to dominate our domestic beer market.

items.title: Australia in danger of World Cup elimination after 'unbelievable' loss to Zimbabwe
items.description: Australia's hopes of advancing out of Group B are dealt an almighty blow as Zimbabwe claims one of the biggest upset wins in T20 World Cup history in Colombo.

items.title: New crew launched to International Space Station after medical evacuation
items.description: The US, French and Russian astronauts are expected to complete the mission in eight to nine months.

items.title: Why this award-winning author's philosophy is 'write like you're dead'
items.description: Michael Mohammed Ahmad, author of The Lebs, marks turning 40 with the publication of his most confronting novel yet.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of Wuthering Heights, Hansel and Gretel and George Costanza's answering machine
items.description: Every question has only two options: One is right and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: 'Nobody is safe' from watchful gaze of Bald Archies satirical art prize
items.description: From the trial of Erin Patterson to the landslide election victory, 2025 is pilloried in this year's satirical art prize, the Bald Archy.

items.title: 'They found her grave': The words a stolen boy waited decades to hear
items.description: More than 100 Stolen Generations survivors have gathered in Canberra for the apology anniversary. The government is pledging new money to help them heal.

items.title: New details emerge of night Labor identity Tim Picton fatally injured
items.description: A man who allegedly killed Tim Picton in a one-punch attack outside a Perth nightclub claims the Labor identity had repeatedly approached his female cousin before being escorted out of the venue because he was intoxicated, a Perth court hears.

items.title: Children's author jailed over 'predatory' sexual messages to minors
items.description: Oliver Phommavanh is sentenced to six-and-a-half years in prison with a non-parole period of four years.

items.title: Coroner finds contentious police tactic not the cause of man's death in custody
items.description: A Queensland coroner finds the cause of Indigenous man Steven Nixon-McKellar's death during an arrest was "multi-factorial".

items.title: Daughter risks life to save mum ahead of 12-hour flood ordeal
items.description: When her mother was swept into the flooding Todd River this week, Alice Springs woman Latarne Wayne went in after her.

items.title: Rain and storms forecast for Qld after record-breaking outback drenching
items.description: This rare desert drenching is the result of an intrusion of very humid tropical air — an air mass — which is now over Queensland, where it will stall for several days.

items.title: Japan seizes Chinese fishing boat, arrests captain
items.description: Japanese authorities have seized a Chinese fishing vessel for the first time since 2022 and it comes against the backdrop of a major diplomatic dispute between the countries.
